title: Ibrahim's Wife Hears She'll Have a Son. She Laughs in One Surah and Strikes Her Own Face in Another.
excerpt: The Quran tells the annunciation to Ibrahim's household twice. The same three-word phrase (awjasa minhum khifah) pins both to one visit — but where Surah Hud preserves her laugh (11:71), Surah Adh-Dhariyat preserves her striking her own face (51:29, a one-time verb in the whole Quran). Two true gestures of one overwhelmed moment.
seo_title: She Laughed (11:71) and Struck Her Face (51:29): One Scene, Two Gestures
seo_description: Ibrahim's wife hears she'll bear a son in old age — and the Quran preserves a different gesture in each telling: a laugh in Hud 11:71, a strike to her own face in Adh-Dhariyat 51:29 (sakkat, a hapax). A corpus-verified reading anchored by a verbatim shared phrase.
